scenario: Floa Reader EPUB render, search, and bookmark

reference.source: Glaso public guided animation, Reader lesson
observedUserActions: Search for a phrase in the book
reference.fidelity: Behavioral comparison only; no Glaso code, binaries, or assets used.

application.name: Floa Reader renderer
application.runtime: Chrome headless with packaged app.asar extracted to /tmp and served over loopback HTTP
application.bridge: readerApp IPC surface stubbed in page initialization; renderer and epub.js were not stubbed

observations.step: Render the EPUB chapter in Reader
observations.evidence: The chapter heading and three paragraphs rendered in the Reader EPUB viewport.
Reader displayed 1 found and navigated to the matching EPUB CFI.

observations.step: Save a bookmark at the current reading position
observations.evidence: The mocked persistence bridge received addBookmark with an epubcfi(...) location.

observations.step: Keep browser chrome visible during EPUB reading
observations.evidence: Screenshot shows Reader toolbar and library/sidebar while the chapter is displayed.

observations.step: Run the same PDF and EPUB flows from the packaged app.asar
observations.evidence: The extracted package rendered the 240-page PDF, switched documents during search, rendered and searched EPUB, and sent an EPUB CFI to bookmark persistence.

bugsFoundAndFixed: The Reader referenced node_modules/jszip, but jszip was only a transitive epub.js dependency and the app package had no direct link. JSZip is now declared as a direct app dependency.
The Reader called rendition.search(), which is not available in the packaged epub.js API. Search now loads each spine section and collects CFI matches using Section.find().
limitations: Chrome headless validates the local Reader HTML and renderer, not the Electron BrowserWindow integration.
The readerApp bridge was stubbed; native file picker, on-disk persistence, and macOS keyboard routing were not exercised.
The fixture has one chapter; multi-chapter search and cross-element phrase matching require more coverage.
No visible app window was created and the existing Just Browse process was left untouched.
